# Policy Adaptation and Training {.unnumbered}

Part IV examines how models are trained and adapted to become autonomous agents. Pretraining teaches linguistic representation and factual knowledge; post-training teaches agency. We formalize Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on trajectory traces, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR / GRPO), and test-time search topologies that scale deliberate compute over tool action spaces.

::: {#pri-vol3-trajectory-post-training .callout-principle title="Trajectory-level post-training"}

**Invariant**: Base foundation models cannot reliably act as agents without post-training on multi-turn trajectories containing explicit scratchpad thoughts, tool invocations, and error-recovery paths.

**Implication**: Data curation pipelines must synthesize and filter multi-turn rollouts through execution validation to prevent compounding covariate shift.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-verifiable-rewards .callout-principle title="Reinforcement learning via verifiable feedback"}

**Invariant**: Long-horizon agentic reliability requires training policies against objective environmental verification oracles rather than subjective human preference models.

**Implication**: RLVR and GRPO leverage deterministic test suites, compilers, and linters to incentivize self-correction, internal deliberation, and backtracking.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-test-time-scaling .callout-principle title="Test-time search and the verification tax"}

**Invariant**: Allocating compute at inference time through deliberate search over tool action spaces can overcome base model capacity limits, bounded by the Verification Tax ($C_{\text{ver}}$).

**Implication**: Runtimes must balance exploration breadth against verification depth to operate along the optimal Pareto frontier.

:::
